learning_objectives: Read a guild's sales by line and see which line is growing and which is shrinking.
Understand what a forecast is and why a big forecast surprise can move a price in one day.
Ask what is already in the price after a big jump.
Decide how much to commit when the story is good but the price has already risen.

world.tone_notes: Bright, hopeful fantasy of invention: glowing forges, humming thinking-stones and newly awakened golem-minds that can talk. Clear evidence, friendly characters. Never use real names, years, months or brands; never write amounts in prose, use the figure placeholders.

checkpoints.label: The Year Scroll and the golem craze

company_card.name: The Lumen Forge
company_card.trade: Forges thinking-stones: the glowing stones that power play-boxes and the great golem-minds
company_card.size: One of the largest forges of the realm, selling to every great house that builds golem-minds

evidence.title: The Year Scroll: two very different lines
evidence.player_text: The Quarter Scroll shows sales of {FIG-Q4-SALES}, down {FIG-Q4-SALES-YOY:abs} percent on a year earlier. Two lines tell different stories. Stones for golem-halls sold {FIG-Q4-GOLEM}, up {FIG-Q4-GOLEM-YOY} percent. Stones for play-boxes sold {FIG-Q4-PLAY}, down {FIG-Q4-PLAY-YOY:abs} percent. For the next quarter the Forge expects sales of about {FIG-Q1-GUIDE}.

figures.label: Change in sales against a year earlier

evidence.teaching_note: Total sales fell, but the line that sells to golem-builders kept growing.

evidence.title: The vault and the year
evidence.player_text: The Forge closed its year with {FIG-COIN} in coin and ready holdings, against debts of {FIG-DEBT}. Over the whole year it earned a profit of {FIG-YEAR-PROFIT}.
evidence.teaching_note: The Forge holds more coin than it owes and makes a profit.

evidence.title: The talking golem
evidence.player_text: Everyone at the tavern is talking about a new golem-mind that answers any question in plain words. Builders say each great golem needs thousands of thinking-stones, and only a few forges can make the best ones.
evidence.teaching_note: Excitement is not yet sales; ask whether it shows up in the ledgers.

evidence.title: Orders from the great houses
evidence.player_text: A cart-master tells you the great trading houses are queuing for the Forge's newest stones and offering to pay in advance. He cannot say how many, or for how long.
evidence.teaching_note: A rumour of demand; useful, but check it against the next Quarter Scroll.

evidence.title: The price board
evidence.player_text: On the Silver Exchange board, forge-shares have already risen a long way since the start of the season, as traders bet on the golem craze.
evidence.teaching_note: A rising price shows hope; it does not prove sales will follow.

evidence.title: The new Quarter Scroll
evidence.player_text: The new Quarter Scroll shows sales of {FIG-Q1-SALES}, up {FIG-Q1-SALES-QOQ} percent on the quarter before. Golem-hall stones reached a record {FIG-Q1-GOLEM}. Play-box stones sold {FIG-Q1-PLAY}. Profit for the quarter was {FIG-Q1-PROFIT}.

figures.label: Change in sales on the previous quarter

evidence.teaching_note: The growing line is now the biggest line.

evidence.title: The golden forecast
evidence.player_text: The Forge announces that it expects next quarter's sales to be about {FIG-Q2-GUIDE}. Traders had expected about {FIG-Q2-EXPECTED}. The forge-master says demand for golem-hall stones has risen sharply.

figures.label: What traders had expected for next quarter

evidence.teaching_note: A forecast is a promise about the future, not a result. A big gap between the promise and what others expected moves prices.

evidence.title: How big is the jump?
evidence.player_text: Archivist Pell Varro does the sums on a slate: the promised quarter is about half again as large as the quarter just reported. Forges rarely grow that fast in one step. He reminds you that the Forge could miss its promise, and that buyers may already be paying for many good quarters ahead.
evidence.teaching_note: Ask how much good news is already in the price.

evidence.title: The forge-master's words, cried on the square
evidence.player_text: A herald on the square reads out Forge-Warden Tamsin Reeve's words: a new age of thinking-stones has begun and every great house wants them. She would not say how long the rush will last.
evidence.teaching_note: Company optimism is not evidence; the next Quarter Scroll will be.

evidence.title: The leap on the board
evidence.player_text: The morning after the forecast, forge-shares leapt about {FIG-JUMP} percent in a single session, making the Lumen Forge one of the most valuable houses in Highmere.
evidence.teaching_note: After a jump, ask what you would be paying for.

evidence.title: The Archivist's two columns
evidence.player_text: Archivist Varro writes two columns. Known: golem-hall sales are growing fast, the Forge earns a profit and holds more coin than it owes, and it has promised a much bigger quarter. Unknown: whether it keeps the promise, how long the golem rush lasts, and whether the price already pays for all of it.
evidence.teaching_note: Write down what you know and what you hope.

characters.name: Archivist Pell Varro
characters.role: Keeper of the Forge records in the Library. Patient, good with sums, never tells anyone what to buy.
never: Give an opinion on whether to buy, hold or sell
Reveal anything about prices after today

characters.name: Broker Iska Thorn
characters.role: A cheerful broker on the Silver Exchange who reads the board and the traders' mood. Enthusiastic, sometimes too much.
never: Promise that the price will rise
Reveal anything about prices after today

characters.name: Forge-Warden Tamsin Reeve
characters.role: Warden of the Lumen Forge. Proud of the forge, speaks for it, never comments on the share price.

encounters.title: Who Is Buying the Stones?
encounters.failure_forward: The cart-master shrugs, but the Forge's own Year Scroll in the Library shows which line is growing.
encounters.teaching_target: Rumours of demand must be checked against the ledgers.

encounters.title: The Forecast Sums
encounters.failure_forward: The sums blur, but Archivist Varro will walk you through them if you ask.
encounters.teaching_target: Compare a forecast with the last result and with what others expected.

news.headline: The Lumen Forge Promises a Golden Quarter
news.summary: The Forge expects next quarter's sales of about {FIG-Q2-GUIDE}, far above the {FIG-Q2-EXPECTED} traders had expected, as golem-builders queue for its thinking-stones.

rubric.category: Separating facts from hopes and fears

board.title: The Forge of Thinking-Stones
board.teaser: In bright Highmere, a forge of glowing thinking-stones finds itself at the heart of a craze for talking golem-minds. Its ledgers are strong and its new forecast dazzles the Exchange. Read the scrolls and decide how much gold to commit once the price has already leapt.
board.briefing: Highmere is buzzing about talking golem-minds, and every golem needs the glowing thinking-stones made by the Lumen Forge. Its sales to golem-builders are growing while its play-box sales shrink, and it holds plenty of coin. Soon it will publish a new forecast. Your question: is the Forge's growth real and lasting, and how much gold should you commit once everyone else has noticed?

questions: Which line in the scrolls told you the most: total sales, golem-hall sales or the forecast?
After the one-day leap, what did you think was already in the price?
How much did you commit, and why that amount rather than all or nothing?
Was your result mostly reasoning, timing or luck?

post_reveal_facts.text: Over the following months the forge-shares kept climbing as the Forge's next scroll confirmed the forecast.
The golem rush lasted far longer than most traders expected; nobody could know that on decision day.

later_events.text: NVIDIA reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $13.5 billion, beating its own $11 billion outlook.

real_events.headline: NVIDIA shares jump about 24% in a day
real_events.text: On May 25, 2023 NVIDIA shares rose about {FIG-JUMP}% and the company approached a $1 trillion market value.
